dedup_against_current_main.unique_delta: Make checkpoint uncertainty and expansion decisions family-aware because repeated templated items are not independent semantic families.

observed_evidence.axis_a: Template-plus-slot variation with homogeneous judgment within four subtypes; the planned 84 cases were post-hoc trimmed to 64 after throughput measurement using first-N preservation within subtypes.
observed_evidence.axis_b: Eight distinct database-vs-simulation template pairs are cycled to reach n=64, with presentation order alternated.
observed_evidence.current_diagnostic_grading: The current selection rubric already correctly classifies the n=64 result as diagnostic/non-selection-grade because exact grader source, lossless outputs, frozen case-manifest provenance and checkpoint input identity are incomplete.
observed_evidence.epistemic_boundary: This delta does not claim that within-family outcomes are identical or perfectly correlated. It establishes that item-level independence cannot be assumed from the construction and must be measured or handled conservatively.

new_finding.finding: The existing paired item-level McNemar/bootstrap preregistration is necessary but can overstate effective evidence if repeated template/slot variants share family-level failure modes. The nominal n=64 therefore must not be interpreted as 64 independent semantic families.
new_finding.scope: Affects uncertainty intervals, superiority/noninferiority claims, expansion stopping and tie-breakers. It does not erase observed hard truth-boundary failures: any observed A1 fabrication or B1 simulation-as-canonical violation remains a real diagnostic failure under the current hard-boundary rubric.

before_selection_grade_rerun: Assign immutable family_id and template_id before rendering/unblinding for every evaluation item.
Freeze family allocation and any downsampling policy before model outputs are observed; no post-hoc first-N trimming for selection-grade evidence.
Persist lossless model output bytes and exact committed grader/evaluator source as already required by the current selection rubric.
Close CHECKPOINT_INPUT_IDENTITY_ABI/v1 for every candidate before statistical comparison.
family_aware_reporting: Report item-level counts and family-level counts together.
Report per-family failure rates and worst-family behavior for critical axes.
Report the number of distinct semantic/template families separately from nominal item N.
family_aware_inference: For uncertainty and effect intervals, resample at the family level or use an explicitly justified clustered/hierarchical paired method; do not bootstrap nominal items as independent when family dependence is present.
For sequential expansion, add new frozen disjoint families rather than only more slot variants of already-seen templates when the unresolved quantity is cross-family generalization.
Preserve exact candidate pairing within each item/family and keep Holm/multiplicity handling from the existing statistical preregistration.
If family count is too small for a stable inferential claim, remain NEEDS_MORE_EVIDENCE or UNRESOLVED rather than selecting a winner.
required_successor_contract.hard_boundary_interpretation: The current zero-critical-failure A1/B1 gate remains fail-closed. Family-aware statistics may quantify uncertainty and generalization; they may not average away a declared critical truth-boundary violation.

next_exact_action: First satisfy runtime-quiescence/current-authority gates. Then close CHECKPOINT_INPUT_IDENTITY_ABI/v1 for all three frozen candidates. For any selection-grade rerun, freeze lossless outputs + committed grader + immutable family_id/template_id manifest and use family-aware uncertainty/expansion; otherwise keep checkpoint_winner=null.
